disease_label_per_paper: Definite catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome in systemic lupus erythematosus with pulmonary emboli, cutaneous/limb thrombosis, axillary hematoma/clot, and gangrene
presentation_summary: 31-year-old woman with lupus nephritis and ESRD on peritoneal dialysis presented with chest pain, shortness of breath, bilateral leg swelling, and bluish discoloration of the left big toe.
ED CT chest showed pulmonary embolism in left upper segmental arteries; labs showed CRP 423.6 mg/L, ESR 87 mm/hr, low C4, positive lupus anticoagulant, and borderline/positive aPL profile.
Foot findings progressed from tender hyperpigmentation and ischemic discoloration to bilateral gangrene despite vasodilator and calciphylaxis-directed therapy.
Skin biopsy showed fibrin thrombi occluding vessels; later she developed a right axillary hematoma/organized clot and a new right lower-segment PE, meeting paper-described definite CAPS criteria.

thrombosis affecting lungs, feet, and right axilla; simultaneous manifestations; histological proof of microvascular occlusion; positive lupus anticoagulant, anti-beta2GPI, and aCL

quality_warnings: aPL tests and biopsy are stored outside ordinary observations.
This case has strong SLE/ESRD/calciphylaxis mimic context; those facts are retained rather than hidden.
CT angiogram showing no proximal leg occlusion is preserved because the limb process was microvascular/cutaneous rather than simply proximal arterial occlusion.
